1.explanation:
• smoke-all/2023/26/4068.qmd – a test case for issue #4068, which the reporter suspects is related to this nav-fill/tabset regression. It shows how panel-tabset styling should behave.
• smoke-all/2023/26/4034.qmd – another recent layout/CSS change (#4034) that may influence nav/tab styling in the prerelease.
• docs/break-quarto-md/github-issue-1034.qmd – demonstrates panel-tabset usage in Markdown and interactions with other classes (including nav-* utilities).
• docs/test-singleformat-html.qmd – contains an HTML-format test bed for Bootstrap navs/tabs in Quarto; a good reference for nav-fill behavior.
• docs/bug-repros/issue-1340/index.qmd – a minimal bug repro showing nested panels and tabsets that can be compared to the current combination with nav-fill.
• docs/test.qmd – a minimal Quarto document that shows basic panel-tabset syntax; useful to isolate the problem to just the .panel-tabset + .nav-fill classes.
1.bug_scenario: The user is combining the “.panel-tabset” and Bootstrap’s “.nav-fill” classes in a Quarto document to create a two-tab panel (tabs “A” and “B”) that should stretch and fill the full width of the container. In Quarto 1.2.335 (Screenshot1) the tabs render correctly: a single horizontal bar under the title “Untitled” with two equal-width panels labeled “A” and “B.” After upgrading to Quarto 1.3.146 (Screenshot2) the same markup collapses: the panel-tabset’s tabs fall back to the default stacked headings (“A” and “B”) instead of the nav-fill tabbed UI. The clickable nav bars, their background containers, and the equal-width flex behavior are not applied.
